bib.title: REFINER: Reasoning Feedback on Intermediate Representations
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 1100-1126

question: Does fine-grained structured feedback from a trained critic on a generator's intermediate reasoning steps improve reasoning performance?
hypothesis: Generating better intermediate steps through structured, fine-grained critic feedback yields better final answers, and beats scalar reward feedback.
contributions: REFINER, a generator-critic interaction framework that refines intermediate reasoning via feedback; outperforms comparably-sized fine-tuned baselines by +13.1, +3.2, +15 pts on MWP, sNLR, MS
The trained critic alone helps few-shot GPT-3.5 (+3.5, +6.8 pts) and structured feedback beats scalar feedback
REFINER outperforms Self-refine style methods using LLM feedback
Analyses: better intermediate steps improve task performance; training with a noisy critic still helps

method.summary: A critic (UnifiedQA-T5-base) is trained supervised on automatically perturbed implausible hypotheses paired with templated error-type feedback. A generator is warmed up on 10% of data, then trained for T=3 iterations to condition on context, its previous hypothesis and critic feedback (oracle critic in training, exploration by nucleus sampling). At inference the trained critic gives feedback until it says 'No hint'.
method.task: intermediate-step reasoning with critic feedback: math word problems, synthetic natural language reasoning, moral norm and action generation

datasets.name: MAWPs / SVAMP (MWP)
datasets.preprocessing: numeric values replaced by variable names number0, number1

datasets.name: Moral Stories (MS)
datasets.split: human eval on 100 random test examples

datasets.name: Critic feedback data
datasets.size: GPT-3.5 synthetic: 30K MWP, 20K sNLR, 30K MS implausible hypotheses
datasets.source: rule-based perturbation (used for main results) or GPT-3.5 few-shot generation
datasets.preprocessing: MS: random verb phrases from context for semantic misalignment, inverse judgments plus WordNet synonyms for contradiction

models.name: REFINER base generator
models.params: 220M generator (440M listed as REFINER base in Table 11)

training.objective: Critic: cross-entropy L(beta) = -log p_beta(f(u)|x,u), u in {z,z'}. Generator: cross-entropy L(theta) = -sum_t log p_theta(z_t|x,z'_t,f_t(z')) over T iterations
training.warmup: generator warm-up on 10% of training data (supervised); no LR warmup stated

other.exploration: nucleus sampling p=0.5, critic randomly picks one of multiple sampled hypotheses

inference.samples: 3 seeds; T=1 with automatic critic, T=3 with oracle critic; self-consistency sample size 5; ReACT 3 reasoning steps
inference.prompting: GPT-3.5: 2 demonstrations per class, CoT 'Let's think step by step'; refinement prompt includes prior equation plus feedback

parameters.stop: stop when generator repeats or critic outputs 'No hint'
parameters.feedback_format: <error type, position (optional), hint (optional)> converted to templated text

metrics.name: Exact match (EM)
metrics.definition: match of generated equation (MWP) or inference rules (sNLR); order-insensitive for critic feedback

metrics.name: Human relevance
metrics.definition: 3 AMT judges, 5-point Likert, >=4 relevant, <=2 irrelevant, 3 unsure, majority vote; Krippendorff alpha

eval.protocol: 3 runs averaged; binomial sign test p<0.05 vs all baselines; human study on 100 Moral Stories examples, US AMT workers paid $0.10 per task

availability.data: public datasets; critic feedback data generated by scripts

prompts.text: You are a helpful assistant for math word problems. We will provide you with a math word problem, and your task is to generate the intermediate mathematical equations as a step for solving the problem and the final correct answer. Here are two examples:

You are a helpful assistant for math word problems. We will provide you with a math word problem a solution (containing an equation and an answer), and feedback on the solution. Your task is to generate a refined intermediate equation as a step and the final correct answer. Here are two examples:

You are a helpful assistant for generating counterfactual reasoning steps. We will provide you with a problem, an error type and a correct intermediate reasoning step. Your task is to generate an incorrect reasoning step based on the error type. Here are a few examples for each error type:

evidence.quote: We trained the critic model for 8 hours and trained the generator model for 12 hours.

results.claim: Fine-tuned UQA-base with the critic in the loop gains +13.1 EM on SVAMP equation generation over the baseline UQA-base
results.setup: MAWPs train, SVAMP test, UnifiedQA-T5-base generator, T=1 automatic critic, greedy, 3 runs
results.quote: Notably, UQA-base benefits most (+13.1 EM) when adding a critic in the loop.

results.claim: REFINER base reaches 47.2 EM on SVAMP equations versus 34.1 for UQA-base
results.setup: SVAMP, UQA-base 220M generator (440M with critic), average of 3 runs
results.table: Table 2, row REFINER base, column Eq. (z)

results.claim: REFINER large reaches 53.8 EM versus 48.2 for UQA-large + PPO and 46.7 for UQA-large
results.setup: SVAMP, UQA-large 770M generator, 3 runs
results.table: Table 2, row REFINER large, column Eq. (z)

results.claim: A trained critic lifts few-shot GPT-3.5 + CoT answer accuracy on SVAMP from 67.1 to 70.6
results.setup: SVAMP, GPT-3.5 (text-davinci), 2 demos per class, critic trained on MAWPs, 3 runs
results.note: Table 13 lists a different GPT-3.5 (code-davinci-002) at 63.5 -> 66.4; main text names GPT-3.5-text-DaVinci-003 as baseline while Table 13 says text-DaVinci-002
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-3.5 + CoT + REFINERcritic, column Ans. (y)

results.claim: On sNLR, REFINER base improves inference-rule exact match over UQA-base
results.setup: sNLR hard (Liang et al. 2022), UQA-base, 3 runs
results.table: Table 3, row REFINER base, column IR (z)

results.claim: On sNLR, the critic gives GPT-3.5 + CoT +6.8 EM on inference rules but only +1.5 on the consequent
results.setup: sNLR, GPT-3.5 + CoT, trained critic
results.quote: Notably, on the sNLR task, for GPT-3.5, we observe that by adding a critic, there is an improvement of +6.8 in inference step generation; however, only +1.5 in the consequent prediction.

results.claim: Human evaluation on Moral Stories: relevant norms rise from 49 to 69 (of 100) and relevant actions from 58 to 73 over UQA-large

results.note: Krippendorff alpha 0.33 for norm and 0.55 for action (low to moderate); baseline PPO relevant 52 for both

results.table: Table 2, row REFINER large, column Eq. (z)

results.quote: we find that REFINER significantly improves the performance of GPT-3.5 and ChatGPT by +3.3 and +2.2 on SVAMP and GSM8K datasets, respectively.

results.setup: MWP ablation, UQA-base
results.table: Table 6, row REFINER base - critic inference

results.table: Table 6, row REFINER base + critic Oracle

results.table: Table 6, row REFINER base + critic data synthetic

results.claim: Removing the exploration phase lowers EM from 39.8 to 37.4, a gain of +3.3 over the no-critic-training model is attributed to exploration
results.setup: MWP ablation, no critic at inference, no exploration
results.note: Text says exploration improves +3.3 over the baseline model; the table shows 39.8 vs 37.4 (+2.4), 37.4 vs 34.1 (+3.3)
results.table: Table 6, row REFINER base - critic inference - exp

results.claim: Training with a critic with under 50% noise is not statistically different from the oracle, while noise above 75% teaches the generator to ignore the critic
results.setup: MWP noise-sensitivity, critic replaced by random feedback with probability epsilon
results.quote: Fig. 4 (a) shows that when training with a very noisy critic (> 75% noise), the generator LM learns to ignore the critic, as there is no difference between using the trained critic or the oracle during inference.

results.claim: At inference, even 25% critic noise makes the generator worse than the trained critic, and over 50% noise significantly harms it
results.setup: MWP, generator trained with oracle critic
results.quote: With more than 50% noise, the critic significantly harms the generator.

results.claim: The trained UQA critic comprehensively beats GPT-3.5 at producing structured feedback (Table 7: MWP 69.5 UQA-220M vs 63.5 GPT-3 175B; sNLR 95.5 vs 34.5)
results.setup: 500 instances per task, GPT-3.5 given 2 shots per error type plus 2 'No' examples

results.claim: With GPT-Neo 1.3B on GSM8K, REFINER gets 23.4 accuracy versus 21.2 for Self-Correct and 8.5 base
results.setup: GSM8K, GPT-Neo 1.3B generator, UQA-base critic, as in Welleck et al. 2022
results.note: The main text points to Table 8 for feedback quality, but the Table 8 printed in Appendix A is the GSM8K Self-Correct comparison; feedback quality is in Table 7
results.table: Table 8 (appendix), row GPT-Neo + REFINER, column Accuracy

results.claim: Error analysis: most frequent errors are Incorrect Numbers for MWP and Semantic Misalignment for MS, and REFINER reduces errors in both
results.setup: 100 random test instances per dataset
results.quote: We note that the most frequent errors are Incorrect Numbers for MWP and Semantic Misalignment for MS.

limits: Only three tasks (MWP, sNLR, moral stories), authors concede coverage is limited
Critic is task-specific, not general; error types are hand-designed per task
Feedback only helps when critic is accurate: noise above 50% at inference harms; critic fails on outputs with multiple mistakes
Generator sometimes ignores or misapplies correct feedback; for GPT-3.5 sNLR the consequent barely improves (+1.5)
Human evaluation on 100 examples with low-to-moderate agreement (alpha 0.33 to 0.64)
Training uses an oracle critic with gold hypotheses; inference uses T=1 with the trained critic, so gap to oracle (66.0 vs 47.2) remains
Moral Stories skews Western; models may keep biases
